resultJson.description: Move pi's --session-dir from a deleteOnExit temp dir to .orca/cache/pi-sessions/, switch PiBackend to SessionSupport.durable with an on-disk probe, wire pi into the shell's session-resume command, add retention pruning, and update ADRs 0018/0021 + AGENTS.md.

tasks.title: Durable pi session dir + SessionSupport.durable probe
tasks.description: In tools/src/main/scala/orca/OrcaDir.scala add `piSessionsPath(workDir)` — `<workDir>/.orca/cache/pi-sessions/`, idempotently ensured via `ensureCache` (mirror `cacheRunsPath`). In pi/src/main/scala/orca/tools/pi/PiBackend.scala replace `sessionsBase = os.temp.dir(...)` with a `lazy val sessionsBase = OrcaDir.piSessionsPath(workDir)` (lazy so bare/test construction with the `os.pwd` default doesn't create `.orca` as a side effect; first spawn triggers creation). Switch `sessions` to `SessionSupport.durable(IdScheme.ClientClaimed, probe)` where the probe checks `sessionsBase / id` is a directory containing AT LEAST one `*.jsonl` file (not exactly one — a failed-then-retried fresh turn can seed a second file; pi's `--continue` picks the most recent, which is correct). Update the scaladocs on `PiBackend.sessions` and the pi-specific wording in `SessionSupport.ephemeral`'s scaladoc (tools/src/main/scala/orca/backend/SessionSupport.scala:176-181) — pi is no longer the ephemeral example. Update pi/src/test/scala/orca/tools/pi/PiBackendTest.scala: the "willContinue always returns false" test (line 198) inverts — add tests that willContinue is false before a commit, true after commit when the dir holds a .jsonl, false when the dir is empty/missing, and that `persistableWireId` returns Some(client id) after commit. Check runner/src/test/scala/orca/runner/manifest/RunManifestWriterTest.scala for fixtures asserting pi's wireId-less "do not survive the run" reason and adjust if they model pi specifically (the manifest reason derives automatically from wireId presence — no writer change needed). Add an ORCA_INTEGRATION-gated test to PiIntegrationTest.scala proving cross-process durability: run a turn on one PiBackend instance, construct a SECOND PiBackend on the same workDir, rehydrate via `sessions.register`, and verify `willContinue` is true and a resumed turn retains context.

tasks.title: Retention pruning for .orca/cache/pi-sessions/
tasks.description: Add best-effort pruning of stale pi session dirs so the cache doesn't grow unboundedly (the issue's open question; claude's own CLI prunes its transcripts at ~30 days, pi won't prune orca's dir). On first use of `sessionsBase` in PiBackend (when the lazy val initializes, or at first spawn), delete child session dirs whose mtime is older than 30 days. Follow the `pruneOldManifests` idiom in runner/src/main/scala/orca/runner/manifest/RunManifestWriter.scala:302-311: fully best-effort, listing and each delete individually guarded with NonFatal → ignore, never throwing into the spawn path. Unit-test with pre-created dirs and manipulated mtimes (os.mtime.set) in PiBackendTest.

tasks.title: Shell resume command for pi sessions
tasks.description: In shell/src/main/scala/orca/shell/sessions/ResumeCommand.scala: change `build` to accept the validated `workDir: os.Path` (its caller SessionAction.resume at shell/src/main/scala/orca/shell/actions/SessionAction.scala:83 already has it from `validatedWorkDir`; `staticGate` and the SessionPicker preview stay workDir-free and unchanged). Replace the `BackendTag.Pi` case's unconditional Left with: compute `dir = workDir / ".orca" / "cache" / "pi-sessions" / wireId` (wireId already passed the blank/leading-dash guard); if the dir exists with a `.jsonl`, emit `Seq(binary, "--session-dir", dir.toString, "--continue")`, else Left("pi session dir no longer exists" — pruned or checkout cleaned), mirroring how gemini's missing index maps to Left. Also update `wireIdAndTag`'s scaladoc (line 15-22), which says "pi always" has no wireId — old manifests' wireId-less pi rows still correctly fall into the generic reason path. Update shell/src/test/scala tests for ResumeCommand (build now takes workDir; add pi cases: dir present → argv, dir absent → Left) and any SessionAction/SessionPicker tests affected by the signature change.

tasks.title: ADR and docs updates
tasks.description: Doc-only task. ADR 0018 (adr/0018-stage-bound-flow-runtime.md) §2.6: update the probe table's pi row (currently "none — sessions live in a deleteOnExit temp dir") to the on-disk `.orca/cache/pi-sessions/<id>/` ≥1-jsonl check, fix the two prose mentions that pi has no probe (R22 text and the paragraph after the table), and add a short dated amendment noting pi moved to durable (follow the existing amendment style in that ADR). ADR 0021 (adr/0021-orca-shell.md): §8's resume-exec table pi row (line ~445, "greyed out") becomes `pi --session-dir <workDir>/.orca/cache/pi-sessions/<id> --continue`; remove or annotate the Non-goals bullet "pi session continuation" (line ~630). AGENTS.md "Sessions" section: line ~120 cites pi as the `SessionSupport.ephemeral` example and line ~126 lists ClientClaimed backends — update both. Grep README.md for pi-session/resumability mentions and update if present (per project convention keep README reference tables intact, only fix stale claims). Note the accepted version-skew answer in the ADR 0018 amendment: pi auto-migrates older session-file versions on load, accepted as-is. Keep all doc edits maximally concise per the user's documentation style.

resultJson.brief:
Repo: orca (Scala 3, direct-style on Ox, munit tests, sbt multi-module). MANDATORY: load the `direct-style-scala` skill via the Skill tool before writing or reviewing any Scala code.

Goal: pi's CLI sessions are already durable on disk; orca makes them ephemeral by pointing `--session-dir` at a `deleteOnExit` temp dir. Move that dir under `.orca/cache/pi-sessions/<orca-session-id>/`, promote pi to a durable backend with an existence probe, and let the shell resume pi chats.

Key files:
- pi/src/main/scala/orca/tools/pi/PiBackend.scala — `sessionsBase` (temp dir, lines 51-52), `sessions = SessionSupport.ephemeral(IdScheme.ClientClaimed)` (line 59-60), `openConversation` computes `sessionsBase / SessionId.value(session)` and a `resume` boolean from `dispatchFor` (Resume → `--continue`). Constructed with the flow's real `workDir` by PiAgents.default (pi/src/main/scala/orca/tools/pi/PiAgents.scala); the `os.pwd` default is test-only, so don't create `.orca` eagerly at construction — use a lazy val.
- pi/src/main/scala/orca/tools/pi/PiArgs.scala — `rpc(sessionDir, resume, ...)` emits `--session-dir <dir>` + optional `--continue`. No change needed here.
- tools/src/main/scala/orca/backend/SessionSupport.scala — the whole session capability. Under IdScheme.ClientClaimed the wire id IS the orca client session id (== the session dir name). `durable(scheme, probe)` takes `probe: String => Boolean` receiving the wire id; probe must be non-destructive, NonFatal failures read as false (handled by `willContinue`). `persistableWireId` returns the recorded wire id only when a probe exists — flipping pi to durable is what makes the run manifest record a wireId. Commit happens only after a successful drain (`commitAfterDrain`), so a retried failed first turn dispatches Fresh again — which is why a session dir can legitimately hold a second .jsonl; probe must accept ≥1, and `--continue` picking the most recent file is then correct.
- tools/src/main/scala/orca/OrcaDir.scala — ALL `.orca` creation routes through this object (symlink guard + cache `.gitignore`/`CACHEDIR.TAG` before anything lands in cache). Add `piSessionsPath` mirroring `cacheRunsPath` (line 65-68). It's `private[orca]`; pi module (package orca.tools.pi) can access it and already depends on tools.
- claude/src/main/scala/orca/tools/claude/ClaudeBackend.scala:102-109 — the durable-probe pattern to copy (os.exists on the transcript path; scaladoc at lines 74-81 explains why probing only known ids is safe: stray files report false, caller re-seeds — same reasoning applies to pi).
- runner/src/main/scala/orca/runner/manifest/RunManifestWriter.scala — no code change: `upsertSession` derives `reason` from `wireId.isEmpty`, so pi entries automatically become resumable once persistableWireId returns Some. `pruneOldManifests` (lines 302-311) is the best-effort pruning idiom to mirror for pi-sessions retention (30-day mtime cutoff).
- runner/src/main/scala/orca/runner/manifest/RunManifest.scala — ManifestSession scaladoc mentions pi as the wireId-less case; worth a wording touch-up in the docs task.
- shell/src/main/scala/orca/shell/sessions/ResumeCommand.scala — `build(s, geminiIndex)` maps ManifestSession → resume argv per backend; Pi case is `Left("pi sessions are not resumable")` (line 73-74). `staticGate` feeds the picker preview (shell/src/main/scala/orca/shell/sessions/SessionPicker.scala:111) and must stay free of live/filesystem checks. Binary names come from `AgentSpec.harnessNameFor`.
- shell/src/main/scala/orca/shell/actions/SessionAction.scala — `resume` validates the manifest's workDir (`validatedWorkDir`) BEFORE calling build, then execs the argv with `cwd = workDir`. Pass that validated `os.Path` into build for the pi dir path; use an absolute path in the argv rather than relying on pi resolving a relative --session-dir against cwd.

Tests: pi/src/test/scala/orca/tools/pi/ (PiBackendTest asserts session-dir argv wiring and `willContinue` false at line 198 — inverts; PiIntegrationTest is gated on the ORCA_INTEGRATION env var and drives the real `pi` CLI). Shell tests under shell/src/test. runner's RunManifestWriterTest may have pi fixtures.

Docs to update (final task): adr/0018-stage-bound-flow-runtime.md §2.6 (probe table pi row ~line 597, R22 prose, post-table paragraph; ADR uses dated amendment blocks — add one), adr/0021-orca-shell.md (resume table pi row line ~445, Non-goals bullet line ~630), AGENTS.md Sessions section (lines ~118-126 cite pi as the ephemeral example). Report line refs 419/581 for ADR 0021 are stale; actual lines ~445/630.

Conventions: comments state usage/invariants, never implementation history; be maximally concise in docs; munit FunSuite; never commit unless asked. Decided answers to the issue's open questions: retention = 30-day mtime prune, best-effort, at first sessionsBase use; probe = dir with ≥1 .jsonl (NOT exactly one — see retry note above); version-skew (pi auto-migrating v1→v3 session files on load) accepted, noted in the ADR amendment.
